paper_metadata.title: Multiplicative-Weights Methods and Gibbs-State Preparation for Conic Portfolio Optimization: A Mathematical Framework Connecting Quantum Algorithms, Jordan Algebras, and Quantitative Finance

experiments.description: The paper proposes a theoretical multiplicative-weights-based SOCP feasibility solver for portfolio optimization, but does not report any empirical quantum or hybrid experiment on hardware or simulator.

algorithm.variant: Theoretical MW-based SOCP feasibility solver with Gibbs-state preparation

problem_formulation.objective_function: SOCP feasibility for portfolio constraints; examples include mean-variance minimization, Sharpe-ratio feasibility, robust mean-variance, and SDP relaxations for cardinality constraints
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Feasibility reduction via bisection; Lorentz-cone constraints; rotated Lorentz cone for quadratic terms; no penalty-based quantum encoding is implemented
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_t is a block-diagonal matrix of violation certificates; for Lorentz cones, each block is an arrowhead matrix M(x0, xbar) = [[x0, xbar^T],[xbar, x0 I]]

problem_instance.description: Generic portfolio optimization formulations over abstract dimensions n, k, r, m; no concrete numerical instance is evaluated

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: The paper discusses factor-model extraction, Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage, and constraint scaling as conditioning improvements, but not as a reported experimental pipeline
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Bisection over Sharpe-ratio threshold; averaging MW iterates or returning feasibility certificates

results.unit: R^2 log(N) / epsilon^2, with T = ceil(4 R^2 log(N) / epsilon^2)
O(d_j) per Lorentz cone block; O(N) total

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic in r relative to classical MW; improved from naive SDP quantum scaling
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical MW and naive SDP quantum algorithms
speedup_claims.conditions: under coherent query access to constraint data and when Lorentz-cone arrowhead structure is preserved
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an asymptotic claim only; no empirical hardware or simulator benchmark is reported. The claimed O(N) Gibbs-state computation relies on violation certificates remaining arrowhead matrices.

speedup_claims.factor: O(d_j) per cone block instead of O(N^3) general matrix exponential
speedup_claims.baseline_method: general SDP embedding / dense matrix exponential
speedup_claims.conditions: for Lorentz-cone blocks represented as arrowhead matrices
speedup_claims.caveats: The savings are structural and depend on the SOCP-specific arrowhead form; general SDP certificates would lose this advantage.

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic speedup in iteration scaling: eO(sqrt(r)) vs eO(r)
speedup_claims.conditions: quantum MW with Gibbs-state preparation and coherent access assumptions
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper labels this as informal/theoretical; practical advantage depends on input model and data-loading costs.
